title: Streaming session eviction and soft-abort protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem overview:

Currently the streaming API can leave partially-generated outputs and ephemeral state in the serving runtime when clients disconnect abruptly or exceed timeouts. This leads to: higher memory/KV cache pressure, skewed billing/observability for stuck generations, and edge cases where resumed clients see inconsistent prefixes (stale tokens or invalid resume tokens).

Goal:
- Define an explicit "soft-abort" protocol for client-initiated or server-enforced termination that reliably reclaims resource-efficiently while preserving resume semantics where possible.
- Implement a session eviction policy with time-based and resource-pressure triggers that minimizes false-positive cleanup and provides observability/traceability for evicted generations.
- Introduce tombstone and staleness windows for partial token blobs so downstream consumers (console, billing, audits) can differentiate between intentionally aborted, expired, and permanently orphaned generations.

Constraints and non-goals:
- We will not change public streaming wire protocol shape in this ticket; compatibility layers will be achieved by adding optional metadata and server-side behavior only.
- This ticket focuses on server/runtime policies and control-plane signals. UX and SDK surface changes (retry helpers, client heuristics) will be follow-ups.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Soft-abort handshake
   - Introduce an internal server message type SOFT_ABORT with fields: session_id, generation_id, reason_code, server_epoch, optional resume_hint_token.
   - When a client disconnects cleanly, server emits SOFT_ABORT and transitions generation to "pausable" with a short grace period (default 60s).
   - For abrupt disconnects or client dead TCP, server starts a 30s heartbeat window before emitting SOFT_ABORT.

2) Eviction tiers and triggers
   - Grace tier: short-lived pause (60s) where generation is checkpointed in-memory and resume token remains valid.
   - Stale tier: after grace expiry, generation enters Stale (TTL configurable, default 24h) persisted as a compact tombstone + minimal KV prefix to enable diagnostics.
   - Orphaned/GC tier: after stale TTL or under memory pressure, fully reclaim KV cache and mark generation as GCed with tombstone metadata (reason: timeout|eviction|manual).
   - Triggers: heartbeat timeout, client disconnect, memory/kv pressure metric thresholds, operator-initiated maintenance windows.

3) Resume semantics and compatibility
   - Resume allowed only from Grace tier. Resume attempts in Stale receive a clear error with resume_hint_token if we have partial prefix cached; otherwise instruct client to restart with supplied seed.
   - SDKs can opt into aggressive resume heuristics but must handle explicit RESUME_NOT_POSSIBLE responses.

4) Observability and audit trail
   - Emit structured events to the console pipeline for every transition (PAUSE -> STALE -> GC) with tags: customer_id, model, route, session_id, generation_id, reason_code, server_epoch, memory_snapshot, trace_id.
   - Add dashboards for orphaned-generation count, median stale-time, reclaim latency, and cost-attributed tokens reclaimed.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 1 (this ticket): implement SOFT_ABORT pipeline + grace tier transition and heartbeat detection. Add structured events and minimal console metric hooks. Unit tests + integration harness (local runtime).
- Phase 2: stale-tier persistence + tombstone compacting and read-path enforcement for resume. End-to-end tests with SDK simulating reconnects.
- Phase 3: GC under pressure path, operator controls, and rollout with feature flag.

Acceptance criteria:
- Server emits SOFT_ABORT for clean disconnects and abrupt disconnects within the configured heartbeat window.
- Generations transition into Grace then Stale state per timers and can be resumed only during Grace.
- Structured events are visible in console (test dashboard) within 60s of transition.
- Integration test that simulates 100 concurrent streaming clients disconnecting randomly shows reclaimed memory within expected bounds and no crash.

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Short grace windows minimize memory but increase resume failures and potential customer complaints. We will roll out conservative defaults and enable per-customer grace tuning for Dedicated/Private tiers.
- Persisting tombstones increases storage surface and retention/config complexity; we will compact tombstones and store minimal metadata only.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Spike: prototype SOFT_ABORT message handling in runtime (Marco) — 2d.
- Add console event schemas and temporary dashboard panel (Priya) — 3d.
- Define config knobs and feature-flag gating for rollout (SRE + PM).
- Write integration tests simulating network partitions and SDK reconnects.
